title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This page is the canonical People Ops handbook entry for 'Working at Redwood'. It summarizes: roles and career ladders, benefits and perks, our hiring and onboarding process, and the core internal tools new hires need to be productive. Use this as a primary reference for managers, new hires, and people partners.

Key principles
- People-first: transparent career paths, predictable promotion criteria, and equitable access to benefits.
- Engineer-centric: documentation and tooling are optimized for fast ramp and self-service.
- Privacy and security: access is granted on a least-privilege basis; follow RBAC and data-handling guidance.

Roles & career ladders
---------------------
Purpose: explain job families, expectations by level, and promotion guidance. Managers and ICs should use these criteria during 1:1s and performance cycles.

Job families (high-level)
- Engineering (serving runtime, infra, platform, developer experience)
- Applied ML & Research
- Product (product managers, designers, PMM)
- SRE & Operations
- People Ops & Recruiting
- Sales & Customer Success
- Finance, Legal, & Security

Canonical career ladder (example for IC engineering)
| Title | Level | Typical tenure | Promotion signals |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Software Engineer I | IC1 | 0-18 months | Delivers defined tasks, learns codebase, follows practices |
| Software Engineer II | IC2 | 1-3 years | Independently owns components, clear design skills, reliable delivery |
| Senior Software Engineer | IC3 | 3-6 years | Leads designs, mentors others, impacts cross-team projects |
| Staff Engineer | IC4 | 5+ years | Technical strategy, influences multiple teams, leads high-risk systems |
| Principal Engineer | IC5 | Senior leader | Sets company technical direction, large-scale cross-company impact |

Promotion process (high level)
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet: accomplishments, artifacts, and manager write-up.
2. Manager collects feedback from stakeholders and fills evaluation form.
3. Calibration panel (peer managers + people-ops) reviews evidence against ladder rubric.
4. Decision and career conversation: promotion with updated responsibilities and compensation.

Promotion checklist for managers
- Evidence of impact (metrics, projects, adoption)
- Examples of mentorship and technical leadership
- Alignment to ladder rubric and competency matrix
- Risk assessment and growth plan if promotion is deferred

Benefits & perks
----------------
Summary: Redwood offers a competitive benefits package designed to support mental, physical, and financial health. Details are maintained by People Ops and updated annually.

Health & wellness
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with company contribution tiers.
- Flexible spending accounts (FSA) and Health Savings Accounts (HSA) where applicable.
- Mental health coverage: up to 8 therapy sessions per calendar year fully reimbursed (check plan for details).

Financial benefits
- Competitive base salary + equity grants at hire, refresh cycles for high performers.
- 401(k) matching (US).
- Annual compensation review cycle + ad hoc market adjustments for critical roles.

Time off & flexible work
- Generous PTO policy (unified policy with recommended minimum accrual).
- Parental leave: primary and secondary caregiver policies.
- Flexible working hours with core hours for cross-team collaboration (10:00-16:00 local time recommended).

Perks & culture
- Monthly learning stipend and conference budget for engineers and product.
- Home office stipend for remote employees and relocation support for new hires when eligible.
- Regular company retreats, team offsites, and lunch stipends for local offices.

Hiring & onboarding overview
---------------------------
Goal: reduce time-to-productivity while ensuring high hiring bar and fair process.

Hiring lifecycle (steps)
1. Role scoping: hiring manager writes a role brief and scorecard in Greenhouse and gets People Ops approval.
2. Sourcing & interview loop design: interviewers selected to cover skills, system design, culture add, and role-specific tasks.
3. Interviews: standardized rubrics used for every candidate.
4. Offer & negotiation: compensation package created by People Ops in collaboration with hiring manager.
5. Background checks and reference checks.
6. Onboarding plan created and shared before day 1.

Interview best practices (for interviewers)
- Use the published rubric (link in the recruiting toolkit).
- Focus on specific behaviors and evidence; avoid hypotheticals without context.
- Provide timely, written feedback within 48 hours.

Common new-hire onboarding milestones
- Pre-boarding (1 week before): equipment shipped, account invites sent, first-week calendar created.
- Day 1: orientation, benefits walkthrough, manager 1:1, team intro.
- Week 1: role-specific onboarding sessions, access to code repos, first small task.
- Month 1: first project ramp, buddy check-ins weekly.
- Month 3: performance checkpoint and 90-day goals review.

Day 1 checklist (manager & new hire)
- Confirm equipment and access (laptop, VPN, email).
- Introduce to team and calendar blocks for onboarding.
- Share team charter and immediate priorities.
- Assign buddy and first small deliverable.

Internal tools & guides
----------------------
Access policy
- Access is provisioned via our identity provider (Okta) and follows least privilege. Request flows are available in the Access and Permissions policy.

Core tools (by function)
- Source control: GitHub (org: redwood-inference). Repos are categorized by team and service.
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions + internal workflows for deployment and testing.
- Cloud accounts: GCP accounts managed under the infra org; access through Cloud Identity and approved roles.
- Observability: Datadog dashboards and alerts, traces in Honeycomb, logs in BigQuery.
- Incident management: PagerDuty for oncall; Statuspage for public incidents.
- Documentation: Confluence (this space) for handbook and design docs; README-first approach in repos.
- Hiring & HR: Greenhouse for requisitions and candidate pipelines; Rippling for payroll and benefits.

Self-service guides (links and quick commands)
- Request repo access: open GitHub team access request in the Team Ops channel with repo and level.
- Create a new service template: use the 'service-starter' repo and run `make new-service` (supports Go/Python/Node).
- Deploy to staging: `./deploy.sh -e staging --service <name>` (CI will run tests and promote).

Security & data handling reminders
- Always follow the secure-SDLC checklist before shipping changes that handle customer data.
- For private deployments and customer data, consult the Security & Compliance playbooks for encryption and key management practices.

People Ops contacts & escalation
- Primary contact: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com) — for benefits, payroll, and policy questions.
- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.com — for interview scheduling and role briefs.
- People Partner owners: listed on the People Ops team page for each org.

FAQ
---
Q: Who do I contact to add a dependent to benefits?
A: Submit a ticket to People Ops via the HR portal and attach supporting docs; use the benefits enrollment period or qualifying event flow.

Q: How do promotions affect compensation timing?
A: Promoted hires are placed on the next payroll cycle; compensation adjustments may be prorated depending on the effective date.
